primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Distal RTA results from impaired hydrogen-ion secretion by alpha-intercalated cells of the collecting duct, including inherited or acquired defects of apical H+-ATPase-dependent acid secretion. Urine remains inappropriately alkaline despite systemic metabolic acidosis, promoting hypocitraturia and calcium-phosphate nephrolithiasis.
vignette: A young patient has recurrent calcium-phosphate kidney stones and muscle weakness. Laboratory studies show a normal-anion-gap hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis with hypokalemia. Urine pH remains above 5.5 despite systemic acidosis.
lead: Which of the following tubular defects best explains these findings?
correct: Impaired hydrogen-ion secretion by alpha-intercalated cells of the collecting duct
distractors: Reduced proximal-tubular bicarbonate reabsorption with preserved distal urine acidification
Decreased aldosterone action causing hyperkalemia and reduced ammonium excretion
Increased sodium-chloride cotransporter activity in the distal convoluted tubule
Impaired vasopressin-mediated aquaporin-2 insertion in collecting-duct principal cells
distractor_notes: Reduced proximal bicarbonate reabsorption causes type 2 proximal RTA; once plasma bicarbonate falls below the reduced threshold, distal acidification can lower urine pH.
Low aldosterone action causes type 4 RTA, which is characteristically associated with hyperkalemia rather than hypokalemia.
Distal-convoluted-tubule sodium-chloride cotransporter activity is not the acidification defect producing persistently alkaline urine and calcium-phosphate stones.
Defective vasopressin/AQP2 signaling causes nephrogenic diabetes insipidus with water-balance abnormalities, not a hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis.
key_expl: Type 1 distal RTA reflects failure of distal nephron acid secretion, classically involving alpha-intercalated-cell proton transport. Because the kidney cannot appropriately acidify urine during systemic acidosis, urine pH remains high. Hypokalemia, hypocitraturia, and alkaline urine promote nephrocalcinosis and calcium-phosphate stones.
objective: Recognize type 1 distal RTA as impaired alpha-intercalated-cell hydrogen-ion secretion causing alkaline urine, hypokalemic normal-anion-gap acidosis, and nephrolithiasis.
